value: stable minus 2 minor versions, raised only in a minor release, declared as rust-version in Cargo.toml and tested in CI

one .github/workflows/ci.yml whose jobs are partitioned by whether a check compiles Rust, never by which check it is. Tier 0 is a single always-run detector job named plan on ubuntu-latest carrying no toolchain, no cache action and no target/ directory: after actions/checkout with fetch-depth 0 and persist-credentials false it runs one bash step under set -euo pipefail that computes git diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-renames --name-only from BASE_SHA to HEAD, so the path list includes the source side of every rename, with BASE_SHA read from github.event.pull_request.base.sha through the step env block, treats every file name as data and never evaluates it, and writes exactly four job outputs - code, web, workflows, docs - as the literal strings true or false and never as any other value, publishing true on all four for every event whose name is not pull_request so that pushes to main and merge-queue entries are never skip-gated. Every output that gates a required check fails closed, whether the check compiles or not, so a path nobody anticipated runs the gate rather than skipping it, and the body makes that structural - code and web start true and are set false only on affirmative proof that every changed path is skippable, a grep exit of 1, never on a match, an error or a test cut short, and workflows and docs likewise start true and are set false only on a grep exit of 1, and every path test reads the whole list from a here-string rather than through a pipeline whose early-exiting grep can end it under pipefail: code is the negation of a skip-list of paths that cannot affect a compile, a package or an installed artifact, with every entry of the package include allow-list R49 owns forced non-skippable because each of them is a packaging input, and with no skip-list entry allowed to match a file any package contains - so the Markdown entry matches only root-level files. Markdown under docs/ and .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ stays skippable through those directory entries, and no entry matches anything under src/ or a member directory, because src/ is packaged and a workspace member that names no include list packages its whole directory; web is fail-closed too - every change that sets code also sets web, because the web member depends on the core member and the root package that hosts the serve binary depends on every member, and web is additionally set by any change under the web member's directory, so the paths R69 names are a subset of the rule rather than its whole; workflows gates only workflow-lint and its pattern contains the whole input of every check in that job by construction - the workflow files, the local actions they call, which live under .github/actions/, and the workflow linter's own config file; docs keys on the prose tree and gates no job in this file, because R82's link check is a step of hygiene, so it is kept only as a literal output that no check whose input another item declares may consume; and a fifth key is added only when some job would be skipped by it that code does not already skip, and is itself written as the negation of a skip-list, or, if it gates only a job that compiles nothing, as a pattern containing that job's whole input. Tier 1 is the checks that compile nothing, each its own cheap job carrying no cache step: hygiene, which deliberately has no needs edge so that a formatter failure still reports on a pull request whose compile tier is skipped, and which hosts every non-compiling check whose input no key contains, R29's non-code formatting slot and R20's two action-pin checks included, as is R82's link check, while R82's rustdoc part is the doc build step of check; and workflow-lint, gated on workflows, which hosts only checks whose whole input is the workflow tree. Tier 2 is the checks that compile: ONE job named check per entry of target-os-matrix through a strategy matrix over os alone with fail-fast false - never a matrix dimension over Cargo features, because the cache action keys on the job id and not on matrix values - running clippy with the feature off, clippy with the feature on, a no-default-features check of the facade, cargo test with the feature off scoped by -p to the non-web packages so the feature-off property is proven rather than assumed, cargo test over the workspace with the feature on, a build of the serve binary and a doc build, as ordered steps sharing one target/, every cargo command carrying --locked, where each cargo step runs under !cancelled() so that one failing step does not hide the results of the steps after it; plus msrv-floor, a separate single-runner job rather than a matrix leg of check because the floor needs only the declared-floor check Cargo's own CI guide shows rather than check's whole step list, verifying the declared rust-version on ubuntu-latest, which widens to every runner by substituting the matrix os expression into runs-on if the owner answers the open F033 cross-product question that way; plus install-smoke, R50's one ubuntu-latest job, whose web leg is a step conditioned on the web output. Every gated job consumes the detector through needs: plan and a POSITIVE predicate of the form needs.plan.outputs.KEY == 'true', never a negated one, and carrying no status function, so that the platform's implicit success() skips every gated job whenever plan fails or is skipped, under either polarity; the positive form is kept for consistency with R18, R86 and the dorny/paths-filter example, because the one remaining empty-key case, a misspelled output name, is caught by lint on the consumer side and by the detector cases on the producer side, and because a consumer that opts out of skip propagation with always() or !cancelled() must read plan's result, never plan's outputs, as its condition; actionlint type-checks the output name and the needs edge but does NOT reject the negated form, so that rule travels in prose to every consumer rather than being left to lint. A failed plan skips every gated job and skipped is a successful check status, so a failed plan must itself fail a required check; this file hands that constraint on without deciding how it is met: either plan is itself a required check, or an aggregate, if R12 chooses one, includes plan in its needs and treats a failure or cancelled result of plan as failure. ci.yml carries no trigger-level paths or paths-ignore filter of any kind, because a workflow skipped by path filtering leaves its checks Pending and blocks merging while a job skipped by a conditional reports Success; its triggers are pull_request and push restricted to main, plus merge_group so a queue's speculative merge still reports; it declares an empty workflow-level permissions map with a per-job re-grant whose scopes are R08's; and it declares workflow-level concurrency with cancel-in-progress true on a group keyed to the workflow plus the pull-request number, falling back to the commit sha when there is no pull request, so a force-push cancels the superseded pull-request run while consecutive pushes to main never cancel one another and keep populating the cache. This file holds no aggregate required-status job, which is R12's, and no release, secret-scanning, devcontainer or AI-review job, which are separate workflow files. Every further check arrives as a named slot under one rule: a check that compiles nothing is a step of hygiene, or its own cheap job behind a path gate only when that gate's key contains the whole input of every check in the job; a check that compiles what check already compiles is an ordered step of check; and a check needing its own toolchain, its own runner or a target/ it must not share becomes its own job with needs: plan and a positive predicate, counted against a ceiling of roughly six cache-bearing job ids per runner, where the budget arithmetic is the sum over cache-bearing job ids of that job id's runner count. Any single-job workflow file that compiles no Rust, R17's scanner included, lands on ubuntu-latest, because it neither shares nor claims a target/ cache entry and gains nothing from a second runner
